To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concentrations of PCBs, OH-PCBs and PCP in the cord blood of infants born in eastern Slovakia were lower than the corresponding maternal concentrations, and the concentrations of OH-PCBs in cord blood were higher than those of PCBs.

the concentrations of PCBs and their metabolites in the fetal circulation are about 10 times lower than in the maternal circulation, and that the ratios of the concentrations of OH-PCBs and PCBs in the fetal circulation and in the maternal circulation are about 4 times higher than in the mother.

the median concentrations of PCBs, their metabolites (OHs) and PCP in the cord serum are about 18%, 75%, and 110% of the concentrations in maternal serum, and that the ratios of OHs to PCBs in the fetus are about 4 times higher than in the mother.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the placental transfer and the cord to maternal ratios for PCBs, their hydroxy metabolites, and PCP, in a birth-cohort from Eastern Slovakia, a region where these compounds are still present in the environment.
the first report of the placental transfer and cord to mother ratio of PCBs, OH-PCBs, as well as PCP in a birth cohort of pregnant women from eastern Slovak.
the placental transfer and distribution of PCBs and their metabolites in the fetal and maternal compartments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the placental transfer rate of OH-PCBs and PCP is higher than the rate of the corresponding parent compounds.
the placental transfer rate is higher for hydroxylated congeners than for parent congeners.
the placental transfer rates of PCBs and their hydroxyl metabolites are different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OH-PCB and PCP levels in cord blood are higher than those in maternal serum, and this is consistent with the preferential binding to the placental transport protein, TTR.
PCBs are transferred to the fetus, and OH-PCBs are more efficiently transported across the placenta than the PCBs.
PCBs and OH-PCBs are transferred from mother to fetus during pregnancy, and that the OH-PCBs may be transferred preferentially to the fetus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OH-PCB and PCP levels are elevated in cord blood and are associated with higher cord to maternal serum ratios, suggesting preferential placental transfer of these compounds.
OH-PCB concentrations in fetal serum were higher than those in maternal serum.
OH-PCBs and PCP are present in cord serum and that the ratio of OH-PCBs to parent PCBs in cord serum is much higher than that in maternal serum.
